title: The Treasure That Never Runs Out

pages.text: The Treasure That Never Runs Out A Story About Natural Resources It was Outdoor Learning Day. Lila and Jay joined their classmates for a hike in Green Valley Nature Park. Their park guide, Ranger Maya, handed each group an old treasure map. "Today's treasure isn't gold," she smiled. "It's something much more valuable." The map led them to a sparkling river, a windy hill, a sunny field, and a quiet forest. "What kind of treasure is this?" Jay wondered. "You'll find out," Ranger Maya said. Did You Know? A natural resource is something that comes from nature. We use natural resources every day!

Nature's Gifts Ranger Maya picked up a stone and explained that a natural resource is anything that comes from nature. Examples include water in the river, trees in the forest, sunlight warming our faces, wind moving the leaves, and rocks beneath our feet. These resources help us build homes, grow food, make clothes, and produce electricity. Did You Know? Natural resources come from nature and help us every day.

Two Types of Natural Resources As they continued walking, Ranger Maya stopped beside a wind turbine and pointed toward the bright Sun. "Natural resources are classified into two types. The first type is called renewable resources. These resources can be replaced naturally if we use them wisely." She pointed to sunlight, wind, water, and trees. Nature keeps replacing these resources. Jay smiled. "So they can be used again and again!"

Resources That Take Millions of Years At the park's Earth Science Center, Ranger Maya showed them coal, oil, natural gas, and metals. She explained that these are non-renewable resources because they take millions of years to form deep inside the Earth. Coal, oil, and natural gas are called fossil fuels because they were formed from ancient plants and animals. If these resources are used up, they cannot be replaced quickly. Lila said they must be used carefully.

Using Resources Wisely As they left the center, Ranger Maya led them to a recycling station. "We can't live without resources, but we can use them wisely." Saving water keeps it clean and available for everyone. Planting trees gives us fresh air and a healthy planet. Reducing waste keeps our land and water safe. Saving energy helps our Earth and saves money too. Jay looked thoughtful. "If we all do our part," Ranger Maya smiled, "our treasure will never run out."

Our Promise to Nature As the sun began to set, they sat by the lake and watched the sky turn golden. "Everything we learned today is like a treasure," said Lila. Jay added, "And it's up to us to protect it!" Ranger Maya handed them a card. "Make a promise to nature, and keep it in your heart." Lila and Jay wrote their promise to use resources wisely and to care for the Earth every single day. "When we work together, our treasure will never run out." And with that, their adventure came to an end—but their promise to nature was just the beginning.

Science Element Natural resources are the things we get from nature that we need to live and grow. Renewable resources can be replaced naturally in a short time, like sunlight, water, wind, and trees. Non-renewable resources take millions of years to form, like coal, oil, natural gas, and metals. Coal, oil, and natural gas are fossil fuels formed from ancient plants and animals. We can help by saving water, planting trees, reducing, reusing, and recycling, saving energy, and using resources wisely. Remember: Earth gives us everything we need. Let's use its gifts wisely and keep our planet healthy for today and for the future.
